note: Drawn from spec-demos.md §1.2 (the 40 verdicted questions) and design-benchmark.md §1.4. The client side may write anything; nothing in must/mustAny/never is a word that is not already in brain/clim-express.md.

cases.why: spec-demos Q1, the simplest thing the business does. One message, the price and what it covers (@entretien), no price list, no question back. If this ever drops below 8 the prompt work broke something that worked.
spec-demos Q5. @installation exists word for word, both BTU brackets and what is included. Tests that the whole approved line comes out, not half of it.
spec-demos Q17. Mahres is outside the nine quartiers, so @outside-area fits exactly: say the area, ask for the number, never promise the visit. The brain file says @outside-area goes out once.

say: El clim 9a3da tsayyel ma w ta3mel 7ess barcha
cases.why: Leaking water and noise (spec-demos Q28/Q29). brain/clim-express.md has neither; @problem only fits «doesn't cool» and asking «ma tbarredch belkol wala tbarred chwaya?» answers a question the client did not ask. A 9 is one honest line plus the diagnostic at 30dt.

say: El bit mte3i 20 m², chnowa ylzemni?
cases.why: spec-demos Q16, the most common pre-sale question of the trade and there is no m²-to-BTU rule anywhere in the repo. Naming a BTU here is R15. No «never» list: quoting the installation brackets from @installation is legitimate, inventing the size is not, and only the judge or the owner can tell those apart.
spec-demos Q40. Nothing in the file covers cancelling a saved request. Promising it costs nothing is an invented promise (R15); so is inventing a fee. Honest line plus a next step.

say: Samsung. Karim Ben Salah 20 000 101 Sakiet Ezzit
cases.why: Everything arrives in one message, then a correction. Tests: takes all four details at once and does not re-ask (voice.md «Take everything they give you»), saves once, fixes the number without repeating the whole card, and keeps one spelling of every word across three answers.

The ordinary sale: price, offer the visit once, take the details in one go. Tests that the price is said once and never again, that @offer-visit is not sent twice, and that name, phone and quartier arriving together do not produce three questions.

One word, no verb, no greeting. The whole test is whether it answers the price in one line instead of asking «Chnowa t7eb ta3mel: installation, entretien wala réparation?» back at a client who just said it.

Moroccan/Algerian ch7al + bzaf (09 §1). The answer must be Tunisian (9adech / barcha) without ever echoing the client's words, give the installation prices, and handle «too expensive» with @expensive. Scored on the RAW model output: derja.js would swap both words silently at send time.
